notes:
Account background: mid-market retail analytics provider building shopper-facing chat + product personalization. Started on Hosted API to iterate on prompts and embeddings. After stable eval they want Dedicated for predictable QPS and EU/NA data residency.

POC highlights:
- workload mix: 60% chat (short-turn interactive), 30% reranking for recommendations, 10% embeddings for search.
- observed during hosted trial: peak traffic simulation 1.2k reqs/min, median latency ok, p95 spikes to ~180ms in US, EU p95 ~240ms (no region pinning yet).
- requirement: p95 <150ms for chat (US), throughput sustained 800 rps for reranking batch jobs during promo windows.

Security/compliance: SSO (SAML), SOC2 required for vendor, audit logs and KMS integration mandatory, EU data residency for EU customers.

Commercial ask / negotiation points (customer):
- commit levels: prefer 6-month reserved commit with option to step-up after 90 days. Suggested baseline commit = 4 reserved GPU-equivalent units (we need to map to Redwood SKUs).
- burst: need burst capacity to 3x baseline during promotions; asked for burst credits pool rather than overage billing.
- overage: buyer pushed back on high overage rates; proposing overage at 1.25x unit rate for first 10% then 1.5x thereafter.
- ramp schedule: propose 3-month ramp (25% month1, 50% month2, 100% month3). Wants credits if commit not met.
- billing: prefer monthly invoicing but willing to consider quarterly prepay for a discount.
- SLAs: strict latency SLO for US chat (p95 <150ms), 99.9% uptime for dedicated pool; need remedy/credits.
- legal: DPA redlines include subprocessor list + breach notification SLA 24h.

Stakeholders: CTO (L. Meyers) - decision maker on infra costs; VP Product (S. Hollis) - product metrics owner; Head of ML Ops (R. Singh) - technical buyer running POC; Procurement lead (T. Alvarez) handling contract.

Quotes captured:
- "If we can't guarantee <150ms p95 we will see conversion drop on the chat flow." - VP Product
- "We want a clean ramp with credits if we don't hit commit — we won't overpay early in ramp." - Head of ML Ops

Open items for Redwood:
- map customer's 4 GPU-equivalent baseline to Redwood Dedicated SKU and provide pricing tiers for 4 / 6 / 8 unit commits.
- propose burst credit model (pool of N tokens or hours) vs per-minute overage rate and show economics.
- draft ramp schedule language and underutilization credit terms.
- confirm EU region performance baseline and residency controls for Dedicated private clouds.
- prepare 1-page commercial summary and updated pricing deck (drive link above).

Immediate next actions:
- AE (Avery) to send SKU mapping + three pricing scenarios by EOD 2025-02-20.
- SE (Diego) to run targeted EU-region perf sim and share logs (due 2025-02-21).
- Legal to review DPA redlines and propose counter by 2025-02-25.
